program: Civil legal aid, housing and mental-health rights

acceptance.scope: Independently challenged conditional recipient health-plus-net-household-resource scenario; counterparty welfare and marginal donation capacity remain unmeasured. Held until combined publication.

what: Mobilization for Justice provides free civil legal advice and representation to low-income New Yorkers.
Its lawyers address eviction, disability benefits, debt collection and workplace barriers, often alongside health and social-service partners.
The organization also uses community education and litigation to address barriers that individual advice cannot resolve.
strengths: Housing, benefit and debt assistance can protect practical necessities for people with mental-health disabilities.
A randomized NYC legal-counsel study supports better court outcomes, although it does not measure MFJ health gains.
Benefit and debt assistance can help families preserve the resources needed for ordinary daily life.
reservations: No controlled MFJ cohort establishes net household resources, sustained health gains or additional outcomes from a new donation.
Government funding, other counsel and a $3.5 million disability-rights grant complicate donor additionality.
Case totals and benefit awards are not unique households or causal welfare gains; household costs and counterparty losses can outweigh benefits.

sections.what: MFJ is one civil legal-aid recipient, EIN 13-2622748, formerly MFY Legal Services. Its services include housing, disability/aging, children and economic justice. [Recipient](https://mobilizationforjustice.org/) The adult mental-health project is the bounded modeled cohort; other portfolio effects remain unknown. [Mental-health services](https://mobilizationforjustice.org/projects/mental-health-law-project/)
sections.monitoring: Ask for a matched-year unique-household ledger recording housing retained, benefits actually received, collectible debt payments avoided, wages collected and job access sustained, with alternative help and all household costs. A randomized NYC study found better court outcomes with counsel; it measured neither modern MFJ marginal capacity nor QALYs. [Original 2001 study](https://doi.org/10.2307/3185408) The 2023 medical-legal trial reported mixed mental-health and utilization effects, so no trial-derived positive utility coefficient is inserted. [Trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37028914/)
sections.qualitative: Legal representation can retain housing, secure SSI/SSD or public assistance, prevent collectible debt payments and recover wages or remove licensing barriers. [Benefits](https://mobilizationforjustice.org/projects/government-benefits-project/) [Consumer rights](https://mobilizationforjustice.org/projects/consumer-rights-project/) [Workplace justice](https://mobilizationforjustice.org/projects/workplace-justice-project/) Count actual additional disposable resources after taxes, benefit withdrawal, rent, fees, travel and lost earnings. Debt face values, salary levels and legal victories are intermediate outcomes. Same-household pathways are netted before the logarithmic conversion, and gain/burden cohorts are disjoint. Public benefits are transfers with taxpayer costs; wage settlements and forgiven debt may transfer resources from employers or creditors. This recipient-welfare comparison does not establish net social resource creation; the counterparty and fiscal scenarios test this limitation. Housing scarcity can displace another household and all such unmeasured effects remain unknown. [Public counsel baseline](https://comptroller.nyc.gov/reports/evictions-up-representation-down/)
sections.cost: The reference retains the historical conditional health calculation: 6.14297 NYC-MSA QALYs per annual recipient expense of $25,609,806, or $41.69 million per ten health QALYs. A separate signed household ledger contributes -0.33641 equivalent healthy years, giving 5.80656 combined years and $44.10 million per better life. These are judgment-led conditional scenarios, not measured expected returns. A $1,000 gift scales to 0.0390 additional mental-health service exposures and 0.00215 incremental legal-stability outcomes under the retained capacity assumptions; neither is a promised client or legal win. Resource priors imply 0.00108 gain-household exposures and 0.0372 burden-only exposures per $1,000. Gain households receive a net $1,200 for one year at a $12,000 annual resource baseline; remaining households lose $25, including time/opportunity-cost consumption equivalents. Gains are already net of winner costs. A 50% positive overlap adjustment prevents adding all economic-security welfare to the same psychiatric stability endpoint; negative costs receive full weight. [Welfare comparison](https://coefficientgiving.org/research/cost-effectiveness/)
sections.funding: FY ended June 2025 gross expense remains the September29 original-return reconciliation: Part IX $25,194,864 plus separately netted event direct cost $414,942 = $25,609,806. Fresh original-return and Schedule D endpoints were inaccessible in this review; this is inherited verified provenance, not a new check. [Return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202620619349301467/IRS990) The freshly accessed FY2025 annual report states $25,118,398 expense, a distinct unreconciled perimeter. Its 9,848 cases are not unique households. [Annual report](https://mobilizationforjustice.org/wp-content/uploads/MFJ-2025-Annual-Report.pdf) MFJ announced a $3.5 million disability/aging grant in July2025, a relevant competing funding source rather than proof of extra ordinary-gift capacity. [Grant](https://mobilizationforjustice.org/news-and-press/patterson-grant-settlement/) No costed current unfunded plan was established. Ask which additional attorney/paralegal capacity a gift buys, the staffing timeline and restrictions; current annual ratios cannot establish a marginal price. Unrecognized pro-bono/clinical resources, public service use and additional fiscal transfers are unknown and separately stressed; no public savings are credited.

model.costScope: One year full recipient gross recognized expense including separately netted event direct costs. Current mental-health exposure retained; other portfolio net health provisionally zero, not a whole-portfolio lower bound. Headline is conditional recipient-household welfare: signed counterparty/fiscal welfare remains unknown, not an established zero. Signed household resource welfare is separate from health; donor-recipient expense is not full social cost.
model.geographicAttribution: 22-county OMB23-01 MSA. g=.98 is a judgment from NYC-focused service, not measured patient residence; test actual addresses before beta.
model.formula: A=sum(t=1..T) exp(-m*t)/(1+d)^t; Qall=N*z*l*e*r*a*b*u*A-h; Qlocal=g*Qall; price10=10*C/Qlocal when Qlocal>0. Separate income I=.5*sum(disjoint households*discounted finite years*ln((baseline+signed net resources)/baseline)*MSA share*positive overlap share). W=health-only editionQalys+I; headline=10*C/W if W>0, else null. Burden overlap share is always1.
model.counterfactual: Existing public representation, other legal aid, psychiatric care and benefits administration persist. e is incremental outcome versus no MFJ among otherwise-addressable clients; r discounts alternative help; a divides legal/clinical partner credit; b captures net extra capacity from gift. Household resources are compared against publicly funded counsel, alternative legal aid, hospital assistance and ordinary benefits administration, not no government support.
model.attribution: l=1 preserves the historical mental-health exposure per whole-recipient dollar; it does not earmark all dollars to the project. z deduplicates/intensity-adjusts reported clients; no separate general housing or Medicaid benefit is added. Financial exposure scales once with b and l; positive gain cohort shares e/r/a with incremental stability and is halved by resourceShare. Burden-only exposure is every remaining additional service household, independent of clinical success. No separate earnings, housing subsidy, debt and benefit additions are stacked.
model.uncertainty: Very weak, judgment-led health conversion and marginal allocation; scenarios are not confidence intervals. Neither the mixed clinical trial nor court-outcome experiment calibrates .06 annual utility or .15 incremental stability. Overlap remains a weak judgment. Delay uses forecast survivors/new intake at service onset, not fixed current persons; no survival through lag is claimed. Financial cohort size, net amounts, baseline and overlap are explicit uncalibrated conditional priors. The reference is not a probability-weighted expected estimate. Clinical-null, financial-only, unknown and negative scenarios are distinct.
model.nativeOutcomes: Legal service -> additional stable housing/income/care -> finite psychiatric utility improvement. Household collectible cash/consumption change and service burdens; gross legal claims are not resources.
model.nativeCosts: Retained whole-recipient annual ratios: 2,500 reported mental-health service exposures per $25,609,806; judged2,000 distinct/intensity equivalents; after50%capacity,1,000 extra exposures and55.125 local incremental stability outcomes. Not a marginal service-unit quote.

what: Mobilization for Justice provides free civil legal help to low-income New Yorkers.
Its mental-health legal work addresses housing, income and access to benefits alongside a much wider legal portfolio.
The highly uncertain conditional estimate is $41.7 million per 10 NYC-MSA QALYs from mental-health stability, charging gross whole-recipient cost.
strengths: The service reaches people whose psychiatric health may deteriorate when housing or income is disrupted.
Original tax-return reconciliation supports a full-recipient cost denominator.
Hospital and outpatient partnerships offer a concrete route from legal help to continued community living.
reservations: No MFJ-controlled study identifies sustained health gains or the response to another unrestricted dollar.
Legal wins, dollars recovered and avoided judgments cannot be treated as QALYs.
Public legal services and clinical partners already help many clients, reducing incremental donor credit.

sections.what: MFJ, formerly MFY Legal Services, is one recipient, EIN 13-2622748. It provides housing, disability, aging, consumer, employment, immigration and family-related civil legal help. The Mental Health Law Project is not a separately priced charity. [Official recipient](https://mobilizationforjustice.org/) Its current program page reports over 2,500 people with mental-health disabilities served annually and describes collaboration with outpatient providers and psychiatric units. [Mental-health services](https://mobilizationforjustice.org/projects/mental-health-law-project/)
sections.monitoring: Track distinct clients, legal need, case intensity, alternative representation, durable housing/benefit outcomes and patient-reported health at 6–24 months. A legal outcome is an intermediate endpoint. The historical NYC randomized representation study improved court outcomes, but supplies no MFJ QALY estimate. [Original study](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/F1782DCB947F50D13325322DDD0A88CC/S0023921600032977a.pdf/the-impact-of-legal-counsel-on-outcomes-for-poor-tenants-in-new-york-citys-housing-court-results-of-a-randomized-experiment.pdf) A 2023 medical-legal trial found mixed health results—less stress and fewer emergency visits but more anxiety and hospital visits—so reduced utilization is not automatically a health improvement. [Trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37028914/)
sections.qualitative: The higher-value plausible chain is legal action preserving psychiatric patients' housing, income or effective benefits, thereby reducing distress and relapse. The model combines these into one stability endpoint to prevent overlapping credit. It does not add deaths averted, rent transfers or citywide policy gains. NYC right-to-counsel is an important publicly funded alternative, although the Comptroller documents large representation gaps; an 89% housing-retention statistic is an uncontrolled outcome, not an 89% treatment effect. [Public baseline](https://comptroller.nyc.gov/reports/evictions-up-representation-down/)
sections.cost: Central: $25,609,806 in gross whole-recipient expense divided by 6.14297 MSA QALYs gives $41.69 million per 10 QALYs. At 2,500 reported mental-health clients, gross exposure is one service per $10,244; after a judged 20% repeat/intensity adjustment, one client-equivalent per $12,805, or 0.0781 per $1,000. These are whole-recipient ratios, not project prices. Incremental legal outcome, alternative-help, partner and funding factors imply 0.00220 stability outcomes per $1,000. Each receives a judged 0.06 annual utility for two years, 2% mortality and 3% discount. Current reach and FY ended June 2025 expense are a forecasting proxy, not a matched-year causal efficiency estimate. Prior-year and management-summary expense sensitivities are separately labeled; neither replaces the reconciled gross denominator.
sections.funding: The latest original return covers July 1, 2024–June 30, 2025 (tax-year form 2024). Part IX expense is $25,194,864; Part VIII line 8b separately nets $414,942 direct event expense, making gross recipient expense $25,609,806. Schedule D lines1/3/5 repeat $25,194,864, but Part IX explicitly excludes VIII8b; that reconciliation does not eliminate event resources. Revenue is $24,245,240 and ending net assets $7,687,646, not all spendable cash. [Original return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202620619349301467/IRS990) [Schedule D](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202620619349301467/IRS990ScheduleD) FY2024 original expense is $22,033,456 and event line 8b zero. The annual report gives $25,118,398 expense, $76,466 below the latest Part IX total; this discrepancy is unresolved and the annual report is retained only as a distinct sensitivity. [Annual report](https://mobilizationforjustice.org/wp-content/uploads/MFJ-2025-Annual-Report.pdf) No current costed unfunded plan was established. The 0.5 gift response and continuation of historical mental-health allocation are judgments; unrestricted gifts may replenish reserves or replace support.

model.costScope: One year full recipient gross recognized expense including separately netted event direct costs. Current mental-health exposure retained; other portfolio net health provisionally zero, not a whole-portfolio lower bound.
model.geographicAttribution: 22-county OMB23-01 MSA. g=.98 is a judgment from NYC-focused service, not measured patient residence; test actual addresses before beta.
model.formula: A=sum(t=1..T) exp(-m*t)/(1+d)^t; Qall=N*z*l*e*r*a*b*u*A-h; Qlocal=g*Qall; price10=10*C/Qlocal when Qlocal>0.
model.counterfactual: Existing public representation, other legal aid, psychiatric care and benefits administration persist. e is incremental outcome versus no MFJ among otherwise-addressable clients; r discounts alternative help; a divides legal/clinical partner credit; b captures net extra capacity from gift.
model.attribution: l=1 preserves the historical mental-health exposure per whole-recipient dollar; it does not earmark all dollars to the project. z deduplicates/intensity-adjusts reported clients; no separate general housing or Medicaid benefit is added.
model.uncertainty: Very weak, judgment-led health conversion and marginal allocation; scenarios are not confidence intervals.
model.nativeOutcomes: Legal service -> additional stable housing/income/care -> finite psychiatric utility improvement.
model.nativeCosts: 2500/C gross mental-health service exposures per dollar; 2000/C distinct/intensity-adjusted equivalents; 56.25/C donor-attributable stability outcomes before geography.
